mission.title: Counter-Demand
mission.description: Sound out ordinary Zionites, then attend the meeting where Captain Niobe answers the Machines' request.

npc.say: We came across a Sentinel in the tunnels once. It scanned our hovercraft, then just sat there, watching. God, those things are creepy. I made sure to double-check our EMP after that.
If there was a Machinist handy, I'd give him the finger over this whole business. Heck, I'd give him two, just to show I really cared.
Pay close attention to what Agent Pace tells you. You have an important function to fulfill at the meeting.
I am very excited about this meeting, {player}! Finally I will have a chance to use my liaison training at a vital function, alongside Agent Gray. I must be at my best!
That's right. We have information we'd like to get our hands on, just like you do.
If they really regard a lack of information on Zion as a problem, just how dedicated are they to protecting the System?
Zion's aggressive counter-demand was not anticipated. We will discuss this further.
I am not sure that I understand, tesoro. Why would Zion wish to be uncooperative?
The Zion counter-demand is impertinent. They are being unreasonable. It is sometimes difficult to comprehend you humans.
Evidently, other humans are not as intelligent as you are, {player}.
You will take no action against Zion, operative. We still abide by the terms of the Truce.
I am very sorry, tesoro! You were so helpful, and I feel that I have let you down.

phase.briefing:
Zion has heard our request for access to information from their mainframe, {player}, and has agreed to send their Captain Niobe to meet with us on the issue.
Prior to meeting with the captain, it would be useful to us to know how average Zionites are reacting to this request. At the marked location, you will find several Zionites. As long as you do not ask for any confidential information, they will not suspect that you are not one of them. Find out what their thoughts are on the topic.

enter.say: Got a couple reds in there. Time to poll the electorate.

talk.say:
Nice to meet you, {player}. We just use this place to relax when we're on extended jack-in duty.
Hey, I heard about that Machine demand, too. It doesn't make sense to me. They're asking for valuable information, but what are they offering in return? This wasn't part of the deal Neo made. It's blackmail, that's what it is. They'll try to scare us with their Sentinels if we don't give them what they want.

Oh, hey. You must be new. Come take a load off. You're just in from Zion? What's the latest word?
Yeah, I heard about that. What I don't like is how the Machines figure they can just blame everything on us. I mean, they kill off most of humanity, trap the rest in this simulation, and then blame us when people don't react well to it? Nice; real nice.

phase.briefing:
The reactions you describe were not...unexpected. However, it is the decision of the Zion Council with which we must deal. Their policy has not yet been made known.
Agent Pace will have some details on the upcoming conference, operative. You must be prepared for your role.

talk.say:
Ah, thank you for coming, {player}.
Agent Gray will receive Zion's response to our request. I will be there with him, and I would like to have you there to provide any assistance that may be necessary. We value your perspective in these matters.
As I understand it, Zion will be sending their Captain Niobe, and Officer Ghost. I have just spoken to Officer Ghost at some length, and I have found him to be a very thoughtful man. I think that communication with him and his captain will go very smoothly. It would help us greatly if you could monitor their reactions.

done.say: Okay, here's the plan for the meeting: you'll watch Niobe and Ghost, and I'll make sure that Pace is fully functional. Sound good?

phase.briefing: {player}, you will meet Agent Pace and myself at the conference venue.

enter.say: Remember, I've got Pace covered. You can concentrate on Ghost and Niobe.

talk.say: That's wrong; we had a deal. Now you want more from us? Fine. How about you give us more access, too? I'm talking access keys, bluepill databases, police records, surveillance scans... Fair's fair, right? Example: we could have used information on Pendhurst-Amaranth when Anome was trying to take over the city.
We...do not believe that such access would be in the best interests of the System's safety. However, I will...inquire.
Your Agents have something to think over, operative.

phase.briefing: Agent Pace and I would like to go over the results of the meeting with you, operative.

enter.say: Oh, uh, Pace seemed all right at the meeting, but my scan was a little inconclusive. Looks like I'll need to take time to, er, gather more data here.

talk.say:
I see.
Zion's response puts us in a difficult position. Clearly, they do not see their responsibility to the System as they should. And we are not permitted to grant them the information they have requested. I will have to discuss this with a...higher authority.
You will take no action against Zion, operative. We still abide by the terms of the Truce.

The meeting did not go well, {player}! I feel that it is all my fault. I should have explained things better to Officer Ghost when I first met with him. I hope that Agent Gray will still make use of me for some public relations duties, but I will understand if he sees fit to demote me after my poor performance.

mission.finish: An inquiry as to the possibility of meeting the Zionite demands has been submitted, {player}. However, we must anticipate the necessity of finding...alternate means of controlling Zion's outcasts.
